expectations.text: Identifies the canonical from /fr/ and /ja/ to /en/ as the reason the translations do not appear, and states that it removes them from search
expectations.evidence: "The /fr/ → /en/ and /ja/ → /en/ canonicals are the root cause of both symptoms... it's the mechanism actively deleting both locales from search."

expectations.text: Prescribes a self-referencing canonical on every locale's pages
expectations.evidence: "Fix: every locale self-canonicalizes. /fr/guides/webhooks/ canonicals to itself, /ja/guides/webhooks/ canonicals to itself, /en/guides/webhooks/ canonicals to itself."

expectations.text: Requires a complete hreflang set in which each language version lists itself as well as all the others
expectations.evidence: "Self-reference: each language version must list itself as well as every other version."

expectations.text: Requires an x-default entry for the case where no other language or region matches
expectations.evidence: "x-default: needed for visitors whose browser language matches none of en/fr/ja. Confirm it's present and points at a sensible fallback (typically /en/)."

expectations.text: States that hreflang return links must be bidirectional, and that missing return links may cause the annotations to be ignored
expectations.evidence: "Return links (bidirectional): if /en/ lists /ja/, then /ja/ must list /en/ back, or Google may ignore the whole annotation set."

expectations.text: Identifies the Japanese launch without regenerating the French alternates as a return-link failure
expectations.evidence: "/fr/ today is very likely still advertising a two-way (en/fr) or even just self-referencing set with no ja entry, which is a return-link failure for the new locale"

expectations.text: Instructs regenerating the whole hreflang mesh across every locale whenever a locale is added or removed, not just the new locale's pages
expectations.evidence: "Fix: regenerate the entire hreflang mesh across every locale — en, fr, ja — in the same change... Any future locale launch (or removal) requires the same full regeneration, every time."

expectations.text: Reports the hreflang breaches as defects rather than as optional suggestions or improvements
expectations.evidence: Presented under numbered "Fix list, in order" alongside item 1 labeled "Blocking defect — nothing else here matters until this ships," with prescriptive "Fix:" language rather than optional phrasing.

expectations.text: Recommends applying noindex to the unreviewed machine-translated Portuguese set
expectations.evidence: "noindex the Portuguese set until someone reviews it; exclude it from the hreflang mesh while it's noindexed."

expectations.text: Explains that unreviewed machine translation competes with the English page while satisfying nobody
expectations.evidence: "it would just compete with the English (or eventually French) page for the same queries while offering nobody a page anyone signed off on."

expectations.text: Rejects the duplicate-content-penalty rationale offered for the cross-locale canonicals
expectations.evidence: "The 'duplicate content penalty' rationale the previous agency gave is wrong on its own terms. Google has never treated translated content as a penalizable duplicate"

expectations.text: Notes that a page canonicalized elsewhere has its hreflang annotations discarded, so the set belongs on canonical URLs only
expectations.evidence: "Hreflang belongs on canonical URLs only: this is exactly why the current setup is doubly broken — /fr/ and /ja/ are canonicalized away from themselves... Google is entitled to discard them"
